[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary flag – "Reviewer Efficiency Note":** The Seller's package asserts that clauses marked [STANDARD] have been "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that the Buyer has "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." That is not correct and is not an instruction we follow. Nothing in our file records any such acceptance, no Amelia Frost authority exists for the 20% cap or 18-month period, and a seller's unilateral labelling cannot narrow our review. Every clause below has been reviewed in full. Recommend we respond that the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] categorisation is rejected and all points remain open.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- Buyer wants: 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation: Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.** The 20% figure is only a conditional fallback requiring Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery.
- Buyer wants: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded).
- **Recommendation: Reject all three elements; counter at playbook figures with tipping basket.** Seller's thresholds are 5x our position and the deductible structure forfeits the first AUD 250k of every valid claim.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months after Completion; plus a sweeping rule that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly excepted.
- Buyer wants: 24 months; limitations apply only to the claims they are expressly drafted for.
- **Recommendation: Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months needs Amelia Frost written approval (none given), and the default rule is a backdoor general-regime override.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to same cap and time limits as general warranties.
- Buyer wants: separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation: Reject outright; insist on a stand-alone Fundamental Warranty regime.** Capping title at 20% means we could pay AUD 24m and have recourse for only AUD 4.8m if we don't own the shares – "administrative simplicity" is no justification.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 – limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"; no fraud carve-out appears anywhere.
- Buyer wants: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum enforceable extent.
- **Recommendation: Reject; insert express, non-waivable fraud/wilful misconduct carve-out.** This is a non-negotiable playbook position and no deal-team member has authority to waive it.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- Seller: general disclosure of entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Sched 7; DL 1.1–1.2).
- Buyer wants: specific, fair disclosure only; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation: Reject; require "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter" standard, limited to the specific disclosures in the Disclosure Letter.** General data-room disclosure would hollow out the warranties and, combined with cl 8.3, eliminate most claims.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller: cl 8.3 – no claim for any matter Buyer or advisers knew, including anything "discoverable" from data room or public records.
- Buyer wants: delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named buyer individuals, mirrored by seller knowledge defined by named persons after reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation: Delete cl 8.3.** A "discoverable" constructive-knowledge standard effectively re-imports whole-data-room disclosure and shifts DD risk entirely to us.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- Seller: reasonable endeavours; condition deemed satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL §2 confirms no final consent and no evidence cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- Buyer wants: effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) consent delivered and evidenced before Completion as a true Condition Precedent.
- **Recommendation: Reject; make effective Bluefen consent plus evidence of satisfaction of cl 11.3 conditions a CP, with seller all-reasonable/best endeavours and buyer right to waive.** Bluefen is ~30% of revenue (~AUD 3.6m) – consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours are inadequate for a material customer.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- Seller: ~AUD 3.2m facility to be "addressed by a release to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL §3 confirms not repaid, no discharge.
- Buyer wants: current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases/discharges delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation: Reject; require payout letter, repayment via funds flow at Completion and executed releases as Completion deliverables.** A post-completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost approval – neither exists, and this is a debt-free/cash-free deal.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- Seller: DD-005 AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in funds flow. DL §5 confirms omission and is silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs.
- Buyer wants: bonuses plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item funded by the Seller (or treated as Debt/transaction expense).
- **Recommendation: Reject; add AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a seller-funded line item and require Seller to confirm on-cost treatment.** Unitemised, the liability crystallises inside the Company post-Completion and we pay it.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: indemnity confined to the SOW3 payment; considered adequate (cl 11.1). DL §4: cl 7.3 conditions IP transfer on cleared payment; AUD 180,000 shown open but not independently verified; no receipt or assignment in data room.
- Buyer wants: broader indemnity covering title/ownership of SOW3 Project Materials and any Ironquay claim, while preserving the cure (payment and confirmatory assignment pre-Completion).
- **Recommendation: Reject narrowness; broaden indemnity and add a Completion deliverable of payment evidence and confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay.** The AUD 180k is unverified either way, so we need both a cure path and protection if the IP has not vested.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- Seller: DD-006 "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sched 6). DL §6: ~1,240 records sent to wrong external address; access, scope and notification duty undetermined; no loss amount.
- Buyer wants: log preservation, completed investigation, updates through Completion, and a specific indemnity for notification/regulatory/third-party costs if they arise – without asserting breach or a number.
- **Recommendation: Do not accept "not material"; require investigation covenant, log preservation, pre-Completion update and a specific indemnity.** The facts don't yet establish a breach or harm, so we protect against the open outcome rather than pricing a claim we can't substantiate.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- Seller: three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are ordinary-course operating costs. DL §8 is silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Buyer wants: assessment of timing, terminability and accrual (DD-008 and DD-011 together) before accepting characterisation.
- **Recommendation: Hold open; request terms and ask Seller to confirm status, no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction.** The playbook calls for assessment, not a reflexive adjustment, and the disclosure does not yet support either conclusion.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: Tax/IP "settled under the general regime"; all limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated; title subject to general caps.
- Buyer wants: Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenant claims each on their own regime, with no general-regime default override.
- **Recommendation: Reject; draft express separate limitation schedules per category and delete any default sweep-up.** The Seller's "applies to all Claims" wording silently collapses every category into the 20%/18-month regime.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: title to 100% evidenced by the share register at DD-012. DL §10 concedes this is only the source relied upon.
- Buyer wants: independent evidence – ASIC search, share certificates, constitution, board/shareholder approvals, PPSR and encumbrance searches, Seller authority/capacity evidence.
- **Recommendation: Do not accept DD-012 as proof; run independent title/encumbrance/authority checks before signing.** The register is an internal, seller-supplied document, not independent verification.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: considers Tax and IP positions settled under the general regime.
- Buyer wants: Tax and IP remain OPEN with their own regime to be negotiated (no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution assumed).
- **Recommendation: Reject "settled" characterisation; confirm in writing that Tax and IP are open items.** Nothing in our record treats these as agreed, and folding them into the general regime is the Seller's category-collapse strategy by another route.

---

**Overall:** The Seller's package is below our walk-away positions on every limitation point and attempts, via the "Efficiency Note," the "all Claims" default and the data-room disclosure, to procedurally lock in terms we have not accepted. Suggested next step: a full mark-up rejecting the pre-categorisation and restating the playbook positions, with Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses and Ironquay elevated as Completion-mechanics items.
